text:
sara: FYI incoming customer escalation (Acme Health). They started seeing intermittent 502/504s and auth timeouts hitting hosted inference in eu-north since ~09:30 UTC. Short sample from customer: 

sara: ``curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"input\":\"ping\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``

sara: Customer says p95 latency jumped to ~3.5s and then 5xx spike. Raising here to triage, tagging oncall. @henrietta

ops-bot: Alert: hosted-eu-north - 5xx-rate increased 4.8% between 09:26-09:46 UTC (rule: hosted.api.5xx.spike) :warning:

aj: seeing repeated upstream reset (RST) and connection timeouts from our edge gateway to transit peer in eu-north in the packet logs. Also some BGP flap events around 09:27-09:34 in provider syslogs.

infra-eng: I pulled flow logs — spikes in retransmits and out-of-order packets on egress interface eth2. Peer AS shows AS64501 <> AS32934 changes.

mira_cs: Customer wants ETA and repro steps. They also reported auth failures (401s) intermittently alongside 502s. Can we confirm whether the auth service was impacted or if gateway dropped connections?

aj: auth microservice traces look OK internally. Most 401s align with same time window but are downstream errors surfaced by retry timeouts. I suspect the gateway lost TCP connectivity to backend auth instances (connection reset / tcp retransmits).

henrietta: Oncall — I'm switching routing for hosted-eu-north to transit-backup policy to reduce packet loss, and enabling aggressive retries at gateway (short window) to avoid long tail. Doing a quick canary shift for 20% traffic now.

sara: thanks. I'll ask customer to run a quick mtr to our API host and share. Also requesting pcap from edge for 09:20-09:40.

acme-ops (customer): here's MTR to api.redwood.example: 
```
Start: 2026-03-17 09:38 UTC
1  isp-gw 0.3 ms
2  transit-peer 15.6 ms  30% packet loss
3  our-edge 18.7 ms  5% packet loss
4  api.redwood.example 19.4 ms
```

aj: that 30% loss to transit-peer matches our packet captures — short microbursts causing queue drops on provider-facing link. Also saw BGP updates with short AS path withdraws around the same time (every ~2m).

infra-eng: opened ticket with carrier (ticket #CT-99214) — they acknowledge microbursts on peering interface, investigating hardware queueing on their side.

henrietta: Good. Keep fallback routing enabled until carrier confirms fix. I'll extend monitoring and lower the retry backoff for auth service to reduce 401 noise.

mira_cs: Customer asked for a packet-level timeline and ETA. Can we provide an interim note: "We routed 20% traffic to backup transit at 09:45 UTC, observed 60% reduction in 5xx rate within ~4m; provider investigating. Will update by 10:15 UTC."

aj: Confirming metrics: pre-shift 5xx-rate ~5.1%, post-shift ~1.9% within 4m. Adding a short note to incident timeline.

ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem if incident persists > 4 hours.

infra-eng: provider updated CT-99214: 'We've applied queue tuning and disabled a misconfigured buffer profile; observing stabilized egress now.' They pushed a soft fix at 09:59 UTC.

aj: I'm seeing BGP route flaps stop after 09:58 and retransmits drop. Rolling traffic back to primary at 10:05 and monitoring.

henrietta: Rolling back routing now. Keeping aggressive retry config for another 10m to watch auth noise.

mira_cs: Customer confirms success — service latency back to normal and no recent 5xx. They requested the timeline and pcap for their SOC. I'll attach sanitized pcap and timeline to the support ticket.

sara: Closing internal escalation — will draft RCA once provider confirms root cause. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
